title: Malcom X
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Malcolm X (born Malcolm Little in Omaha, 1925), tracing his childhood after his father's death, his criminal years, prison conversion to the Nation of Islam under Elijah Muhammad, his rise as the group's spokesman, his split with Elijah Muhammad over the latter's out-of-wedlock children and comments on Kennedy's assassination, his Hajj and Sunni turn, his meeting with Martin Luther King Jr., his assassination in Harlem in February 1965, and his legacy in books and film. The episode closes with a listener mail about the Magnises credit card.
topics: Kennedy assassination chickens coming home to roost

segments.title: Opening banter and Malcolm X introduction
segments.summary: Hosts discuss their personal familiarity with Malcolm X, the Spike Lee film, his autobiography, and why he was not taught in school, and preview the episode.

segments.title: Childhood, family and father's death
segments.summary: Malcolm Little is born in Omaha in 1925 into a Black-conscious family; his father Earl Little's involvement with the Universal Negro Improvement Association, the family's Lansing-area home burned by white men, and Earl's death by streetcar, which was ruled a suicide but believed by the family to be murder.

segments.title: Mother's institutionalization and siblings in foster care
segments.summary: Louise Little receives a small insurance payment, is denied the larger claim, has a breakdown and is committed to a Kalamazoo state hospital, and the eight children are split up in the foster system.

segments.title: Early crime, school and Harlem years
segments.summary: Malcolm steals as a child to support the family, is sent to a juvenile detention center in Mason, Michigan, is elected class president, and then quits school after a teacher discourages his law ambitions. He moves to Boston and then Harlem, where he earns the name Detroit Red, and turns to petty crime, drugs, gambling and sex work.

segments.title: Burglary arrest and prison sentence
segments.summary: Malcolm is arrested several times and is finally convicted for a series of burglaries with a small crew; he and Malcolm Jarvis receive long sentences while the white women get light treatment, and the hosts describe pressure to falsely implicate the men in rape.

segments.title: Prison reading and conversion to Nation of Islam
segments.summary: In prison, Malcolm becomes a voracious reader at MCI Norfolk, is introduced to Elijah Muhammad's teachings through family and letters, adopts ascetic practices, and drops the name Little for X as a rejection of a slave name.

segments.title: Nation of Islam theology and white devil teaching
segments.summary: The hosts explain how the Nation of Islam differs from orthodox Islam, including the teaching of Yacub and the white devils, a six-thousand-year period expected to end around 1970, and how that fed white fears of a race war.
topics: Nation of Islam vs orthodox Islam

segments.title: Parole, recruiting and growth of the Nation of Islam
segments.summary: Malcolm is paroled in 1952, joins Temple Number One in Detroit, and recruits heavily; membership grows from about 400 to about 75,000 by the early 1960s. He is seen as the group's face.

segments.title: Media strategy, Mohammad Speaks and marriage to Betty Sanders
segments.summary: Malcolm pushes strict discipline in Philadelphia, marries civil rights activist Betty Sanders in 1958, and founds the newspaper Mohammad Speaks; Mike Wallace's documentary The Hate That Hate Produced helped raise the group's profile.

segments.title: Debates, separatism and Malcolm's stance against civil rights
segments.summary: Malcolm debates at Oxford and Harvard and takes questions from reporters, going beyond Elijah Muhammad's wishes. The hosts discuss the Nation's separatism and its refusal to join the civil rights movement.

segments.title: Malcolm X versus Martin Luther King Jr. and the media rivalry
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the media framing of Malcolm X and King as opposites, Malcolm's antisemitic views at times, his criticism of King and the March on Washington, and the federal and NYPD interest in him, including Truman-era correspondence and a Harlem protest where he dispersed a crowd.
topics: Martin Luther King vs Malcolm X

segments.title: Malcolm X's philosophy of self-help and Black nationalism
segments.summary: Josh summarizes Malcolm's message, drawn from speeches such as The Ballot or the Bullet, that Black people must do for themselves through moral uplift and Black nationalism rather than integration.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Break before the discussion of the split from the Nation of Islam.

segments.title: Split from Nation of Islam
segments.summary: Jealousy within the Nation of Islam leads to conflict. Malcolm confronts Elijah Muhammad in 1963 about his out-of-wedlock children, then comments on Kennedy's assassination as chickens coming home to roost, is suspended, and stays in Miami with Cassius Clay before Clay's public announcement, where Elijah Muhammad did not invite him. He then publicly claims Elijah Muhammad fathered children with secretaries.

segments.title: Hajj pilgrimage, name change and reconciliation with King
segments.summary: After the Hajj to Mecca in 1964, Malcolm adopts the name El-Hajj Malik El-Shabazz and Sunni Islam, announces a new view of white people, founds the Organization of Afro American Unity, takes the struggle to the UN, and meets Martin Luther King Jr. in the Capitol hallway during the Civil Rights Act debate.
topics: meeting with Martin Luther King Jr.

segments.title: Assassination in Harlem and funeral
segments.summary: Malcolm's house is firebombed in February 1965 after the Nation of Islam evicts the family, then he is shot and killed on February 21, 1965 at an OAAU meeting in Harlem in front of his family. Three men are convicted, and two are later exonerated in 2021. Ossie Davis leads the funeral, which draws about 1,500 people.

segments.title: Legacy, Betty Shabazz and daughters
segments.summary: The hosts reflect on the roughly decade-long span of Malcolm's public impact, Maya Angelou's praise for his ability to change his views publicly, and the book's sales, the film's box office and Oscar nominations, and its 2010 National Film Registry listing.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts close the Malcolm X discussion and recommend the autobiography, speeches, and documentaries.

segments.title: Listener mail about Magnises
segments.summary: Listener Kevin describes his experience as a Magnises credit card member in New York, including dubious event perks and a quick membership refund, in response to the earlier episode on the Fyre Festival debacle.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Standard sign-off and podcast credits.
